title: The Friday Overage (demo)
idea: Demo of: an invented bakery till is over by the same sum every Friday and the owner does not want it counted (fiction)

spine.want: Iris wants the till to balance so she can close the shop and go home
spine.obstacle: the owner insists the extra money is nothing and tells her to stop counting
spine.turn: she sees that the same customer pays in every Friday and the owner never charges him
spine.choice: she keeps counting and writes down the next Friday
spine.opening_image: Iris alone at the bakery counter with the till drawer open
spine.ending_image: the same till drawer, closed, and her notebook open beside it

cast.name: Iris
cast.look: young woman in a magenta shirt and dark skirt, hair in a bun

cast.name: Mr. Pell
cast.look: heavy-set older man in a grey-green shirt, grey hair

scenes.title: Forty-seven
scenes.goal: Iris wants the till to balance
scenes.turn: the same extra sum has now come seven Fridays in a row

cues.t: Every Friday, the till came out forty-seven dollars over.
Iris counted it twice. Money does not appear by accident.
So she wrote the number in a small notebook.
Seven weeks. Seven Fridays. The same forty-seven.
Somebody was paying in. Who pays a bakery extra?

scenes.title: Close the till
scenes.goal: Iris wants an answer from the owner
scenes.turn: he orders her to stop counting, which tells her the money matters

lines.t: Mr. Pell, the till is over again. Forty-seven, like always.
Well, you counted wrong. Close up and go home, Iris.
Seven Fridays in a row. Same sum. To the cent.
Well, good customers round up. Leave it alone, Iris.
Go home. And don't count the Friday till again.

cues.t: Why would an owner refuse to count money that somebody handed him for free?
